Theme

Latin word

prō

preposition with the ablative

in front of, before (a building, a camp, a gate); instead of, in place of, for; in proportion to, relative to

In this lexicon

  • in front of

    also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 3.27: sedēns prō aede Castoris (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 4.32: prō portīs castrōrum (Lewis & Short); Traupman 278, 319

  • instead

    the recommended word · classical · Plaut. Most. 1131b: ego ībō prō tē, sī tibi nōn libet; Ter. And. 200: ego prō tē molam; Traupman 333: instead of, prō (+ abl)

  • relatively

    also used · classical · Liv. 21.29: atrōcius quam prō numerō pugnantium (Lewis & Short); Cic. Sen. 27: agere prō vīribus (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Quīn venīs? — Prōmitte: ego ībō prō tē, sī tibi nōn libet.

    Why won’t you come? — Say yes: I’ll go instead of you, if you don’t feel like it.Plaut. Most. 1131–1131b
